title: Ethnographic usage tilt map & competitor dossier: operator behavior and deployment signals
creator: Anita Rao
description: Synthesize qualitative and quantitative signals about how customers and operator teams choose, configure, and fall back between models (hosted, dedicated, private). Produce a compact dossier per top-6 competing providers that documents: deployment patterns, common failure / fallback triggers, quantization / infra preferences, pricing/latency tradeoffs observed in the wild, and buyer language (what procurement teams ask). Deliver an "ethnographic tilt map" that visualizes the contexts where each provider is favored (low-latency edge, regulated private install, cost-first batch workloads, etc.).
acceptance_criteria: 6 competitor dossiers (one-pagers) covering deployment and ops signals
Ethnographic tilt map PDF and interactive Miro with per-region overlays
Signal taxonomy for telemetry collection (20+ signal definitions) to feed the model-scout system
Prioritized list of 12 hypotheses for product experiments (rollouts/fallback policies/cost-optimizations)
Hand-off to engineering with 3 example dashboards and instrumentation spec
tasks: Run 12 buyer & operator interviews (recruit via solutions and sales)
Aggregate telemetry from usage-telemetry bucket for Q4 2024 / Q1 2025
Map procurement docs and RFP language to observable metrics
Draft one-page dossiers for top-6 competitors and internal discussion notes
Create tilt-map artefact in Miro and export PDF
Identify 20 signals and write instrumentation spec for eng
Prioritize hypotheses and create experiment canvas for each
notes: Trade-off: depth vs breadth — we prioritize top-6 competitors based on customer mentions and procurement frequency rather than exhaustive coverage
We will anonymize customer quotes in deliverables and surface full transcripts to Solutions only
Sampling bias risk: interviewee set likely skewed to enterprise customers — include at least 3 mid-market users
Instrumentation must avoid PII; work with security for telemetry schema review if required
